theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: How does a temporary hair colour work on the hair?
options: It goes deep into the cortex and changes the natural pigment for good
It lightens the natural pigment first, then adds a new shade
It coats the outside of the hair and washes out at the next shampoo
It breaks bonds inside the hair so that the new colour locks in

questions.stem: Which of these is a temporary colour product?
options: A coloured hair spray or hair mascara
A permanent tint mixed with peroxide developer
A bleach powder mixed with developer
A sodium hydroxide relaxer cream

questions.stem: Shanice has dark brown hair and wants to look blonde for one night using a temporary colour. What should you tell her?
options: It will work if the colour is left on twice as long
It will work if you blow-dry the colour in with high heat
It will work if you put on two layers of the rinse
It cannot lighten hair, because it only adds colour on top

questions.stem: How long does a true temporary colour usually last?
options: Until the new growth shows, in about six weeks
Until the hair is next shampooed
Until the ends are trimmed off
Until the client has a relaxer

questions.stem: What is the main difference between temporary and semi-permanent colour?
options: Semi-permanent goes a little way into the hair and lasts several shampoos
Semi-permanent is always mixed with a strong developer so that it can lighten
Temporary colour lasts longer because it sits on the outside
Temporary colour can only be used on hair that has been relaxed

questions.stem: Why do you ask a client about past colour and chemical services at the consultation?
options: So that you can charge more for the service
So that you can decide which music to play
Because past treatments change how the hair takes colour
Because every client must show a receipt for past services

questions.stem: When must you carry out a skin test before a temporary colour?
options: Never, because temporary colour cannot cause a reaction
Only when the client asks you for one
Only after the colour has already been applied
Whenever the maker's instructions say one is needed

questions.stem: Where the maker requires a skin test, when is it done?
options: Five minutes before the colour is applied, at the basin
Ahead of the service, as long before as the maker says
The day after the colour service is finished
Only once in the client's whole life

questions.stem: What does a strand test show before you use a temporary colour on porous, lightened hair?
options: How long the client's hair will take to grow
How the colour will take and whether it will stain
Whether the client is allergic to the shampoo
Whether the scalp is too oily for any colour

questions.stem: Where is a skin test usually placed?
options: On the ends of the hair at the nape
On the palm of the client's hand, near the wrist
On one of the client's fingernails
Behind the ear or in the crook of the elbow

questions.stem: At the check time, the skin test area is red, itchy and swollen. What should you do?
options: Do not apply the colour, record it and advise her to see a doctor
Apply the colour anyway but rinse it off sooner than the maker says
Apply a different shade of the same product instead
Wash the area and then apply the colour as planned

questions.stem: Before you apply colour, you find small cuts and scratches (abrasions) on the client's scalp. What should you do?
options: Cover the cuts with barrier cream and carry on
Apply the colour only around the cuts, not on them
Do not colour today, and rebook once the scalp has healed
Apply the colour but tell the client not to scratch

questions.stem: Which scalp condition means you must NOT do the colour service, and should refer the client to a doctor?
options: A dry scalp with a few small flakes
Hair that is fine and soft to touch
Ringworm of the scalp (tinea capitis)
Natural hair with a tight curl pattern

questions.stem: Which is the best way to choose a shade with the client?
options: Pick the shade you like best and surprise her
Use a shade chart in good light and agree it together
Choose the shade a friend of hers had at the salon last week
Use whichever colour is nearest on the shelf

questions.stem: On the colour wheel, which colour cancels out unwanted yellow tones?
options: Violet
Orange
Red
Green

questions.stem: On the colour wheel, which colour cancels out unwanted red tones?
options: Yellow
Orange
Violet
Green

questions.stem: What are the three primary colours in hair colour theory?
options: Green, orange and violet
Black, white and grey
Red, green and white
Red, yellow and blue

questions.stem: In hair colour, what does 'depth' (level) describe?
options: How light or dark the colour is
How warm or cool the colour looks
How long the colour will last
How thick each strand of hair is

questions.stem: In hair colour, what does 'tone' describe?
options: How light or dark the colour is
The shade you see, such as gold, red or ash
How quickly the colour washes out of the hair
How much hair grows on the head

questions.stem: On the usual 1 to 10 scale for natural hair depth, what does level 1 stand for?
options: Lightest blonde
Medium brown
Black
Grey

questions.stem: Why do you put barrier cream along the hairline and on the ears before colouring?
options: To stop the colour from staining the skin
To help the colour soak deeper into the hair shaft
To make the client's skin feel warmer
To keep the hair from tangling

questions.stem: How should the client's clothes be protected before a temporary colour?
options: With a thin paper towel tucked into the collar
With no cover, because temporary colour does not stain
With a gown only, and no towel at all
With a gown, a towel and a waterproof colour cape

questions.stem: Why should the stylist wear disposable gloves to apply colour?
options: So that the colour goes on more smoothly
So that the client does not feel cold hands
To protect the skin from stains and irritation
Because gloves make the colour last longer

questions.stem: Most colour rinses and mousses are put on hair in which state?
options: Dirty, with old styling products still in it
Shampooed and towel-dried, as the maker says
Soaking wet, straight from the basin
Dry, with heavy oil sprayed on first

questions.stem: When is a colour spray usually applied?
options: Before the shampoo, so that it has time to soak in
On dry, styled hair, at the end of the service
During the conditioning treatment
Under a hot dryer while the hair is wet

questions.stem: Why do you hold a colour spray at the distance the maker gives, and shield the client's face?
options: So that the can lasts longer and costs the salon less
So that the colour dries a darker shade
To get an even coat and keep spray off the skin and eyes
So that the hair holds its curl for longer

questions.stem: How do you get an even result with a colour rinse?
options: Pour it all on the crown and let it run down
Apply it only to the ends and leave the roots uncoloured
Rub it in with a dry towel to spread it
Apply it section by section, then comb it through

questions.stem: A temporary colour mousse tells you to leave it on for a set time. How long do you leave it?
options: For the time the maker's instructions give
Until the client says she is bored
Overnight, for the strongest colour
As long as you are busy with another client

questions.stem: Mrs Grant has a little grey hair and chooses a temporary rinse. What will the rinse do?
options: Turn the grey hair back to its natural colour for good
Lighten the dark hair so that it matches the grey
Make the grey hair grow more slowly
Blend or tone the grey until the next shampoo

questions.stem: Why may tightly coiled natural hair take temporary colour unevenly?
options: Because coily hair has no cuticle at all
Because the coils are often drier and more porous in places
Because natural hair always pushes all water and products away
Because coily hair is always very oily

questions.stem: How should colour be worked into thick, coily natural hair?
options: In small sections, with fingers or a wide-tooth comb
In one large section, with a fine-tooth comb pulled hard
With a hot flat iron straight after each stroke
With a stiff brush dragged hard from root to end

questions.stem: Damion has locs and wants a colour gel for a carnival event. What should you check first?
options: That the locs have all been cut to the same length
That he has had a relaxer in the last month
That the product will rinse out of locs, with a strand test
That the locs are soaking wet when you finish

questions.stem: Why can temporary colour last longer than planned on bleached hair?
options: Bleached hair is stronger and holds on to everything
Bleached hair has a sealed cuticle that traps colour
Very porous hair soaks up the colour and may hold a stain
Bleached hair is always oily, so colour sticks to it

questions.stem: How should aerosol colour sprays be stored?
options: Upright, in a cool place away from heat and flames
On a sunny window sill so that they stay warm
Next to the hood dryer so they are close to hand
With the cap off so that the nozzle does not clog up

questions.stem: Why should the salon be well ventilated when colour sprays are used?
options: To make the colour dry a darker shade
So that people do not breathe in the spray
So that the spray spreads further across the room
To keep the products cold and fresh

questions.stem: Colour gets into a client's eye. What is the first thing to do?
options: Rub the eye firmly with a dry towel
Put a drop of conditioner in the eye
Tell her to keep the eye shut tight until the stinging stops
Rinse the eye gently with plenty of clean, cool water

questions.stem: What does a safety data sheet (SDS) for a colour product tell you?
options: The hazards, safe handling, storage and first aid
The price of the product and where to buy more of it
Which shades are most popular this year
How to book clients for colour services

questions.stem: After the service, what should you do with the tint bowls and applicator brushes?
options: Leave them in the basin until the end of the week
Wipe them with the client's used towel and put them away
Wash them clean, then disinfect them before next use
Throw them in the general bin after one use

questions.stem: What is the difference between cleaning and disinfecting?
options: They are the same thing with two different names
Cleaning kills all germs and disinfecting removes dirt
Disinfecting is only needed once a month
Cleaning removes dirt; disinfecting then kills most germs

questions.stem: Which aftercare advice should you give after a temporary colour?
options: Swim in the sea straight away to set the colour
Colour may rub off on pillows and clothes, and run in rain or sweat
Shampoo twice a day so that the colour lasts
Sleep with the hair wet and covered so the colour sinks in deeper

questions.stem: What should go on the client record card after the service?
options: Only the client's name and phone number, nothing more
The product, shade, test results and the result
The names of the other clients booked that day
The time the client left and the tip she gave

questions.stem: Colour has stained the client's skin at the hairline. What should you do?
options: Scrub it hard with a nail brush
Leave it, because it will fade in a few minutes
Rub a little bleach on it to lift the stain
Remove it gently with a stain remover, as the maker says

questions.stem: The colour looks patchy when you finish. What is the most likely cause?
options: It was not spread evenly through every section
The client's hair was cut too recently
The salon was too cool during the whole service
The shade was chosen from a shade chart

questions.stem: Why do you show the client the result in the mirror and ask what she thinks?
options: To get her to pay before she leaves
To make the service last a little longer
To check she is happy and deal with any concerns
To practise your speaking skills in front of others

questions.stem: Which statement about mixing colour products is correct?
options: Mix two brands together to get a stronger colour
Add peroxide to a temporary colour to make it last longer
Never mix brands; use each product as its maker says
Mix the colour with shampoo to make it go further

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

On the colour wheel, which colour cancels out unwanted orange tones?
Name the outer layer of the hair that a temporary colour coats.
What cream is put along the hairline and on the ears to stop colour staining the skin?

What is the name of the natural pigment that gives hair its colour?

essays.stem: Describe how you carry out a consultation for a temporary colour service. Say what you ask, what you look at, and what you agree with the client.
essays.modelAnswer: I sit the client in good light and talk face to face. I ask what result she wants and what the colour is for, for example a weekend event or covering a little grey. I ask about past colour, relaxers, henna and other chemical services, and about any allergy or reaction to hair products. I look at the hair and scalp: the natural depth, any grey, the porosity and condition, and whether there are cuts, sores, flaking or signs of infection. I explain that temporary colour only adds colour on top, cannot lighten, and will wash out at the next shampoo, and that it may rub off in rain or sweat. We choose the shade together from a shade chart. I check whether the maker requires a skin test or strand test and book them. I write everything on the record card and ask the client to agree the plan and the price.
markingPoints: Asks about the wanted result and past chemical services, henna or reactions
Looks at the hair and scalp: depth, grey, porosity and any cuts, sores or infection
Explains what temporary colour can and cannot do, and how long it lasts
Chooses the shade with the client from a shade chart in good light
Checks which tests the maker requires, records the consultation and agrees the plan

essays.stem: Explain how and why you carry out a skin test and a strand test before a colour service, when the maker requires them. Say what you do with each result.
essays.modelAnswer: A skin test checks whether the client is allergic to the product. Where the maker requires one, I do it ahead of the service, as long before as the maker says (often 48 hours). I clean a small area behind the ear or in the crook of the elbow, put on a little of the product as the maker's instructions say, and let it dry. I tell the client to wash it off and contact the salon at once if it itches, burns or swells. At the check time, if the skin is red, swollen, sore or itchy, the test is positive: I do not do the service, I record it and advise her to see a doctor. If there is no reaction, I record a negative result and go ahead. A strand test is done on a small section of hair, often at the nape, or on cut hair. It shows how the colour will look, how long to leave it, and whether porous hair will hold a stain. If the result is poor, I change the plan.
markingPoints: Skin test checks for allergy; done ahead of the service, as long before as the maker says
Correct place and method: clean skin behind the ear or inside the elbow, product as the maker says
Positive reaction (red, itchy, swollen): no service, record it, refer to a doctor
Strand test on a small section shows the result, timing and staining on porous hair
Both results written on the record card

essays.stem: Explain why you check the scalp for cuts, abrasions and other problems before applying colour. Give three things that would stop the service and say what you would do.
essays.modelAnswer: Colour and other hair products can get into broken skin and cause stinging, burning, a reaction or an infection. So before any colour I part the hair in sections and look closely at the whole scalp and hairline. I would not go ahead if I found cuts, scratches or abrasions, for example from hard scratching or tight braids. I would not colour over an infection such as ringworm (tinea capitis), impetigo or head lice, because these can spread to other clients and need treatment. I would also stop if the client had a positive skin test or has reacted to hair colour before, or if the scalp is swollen, very red or sore. In each case I explain kindly to the client why I cannot do the service today, without trying to diagnose a disease. I advise her to see a doctor or pharmacist where needed, record what I found on the record card, and offer to rebook once the scalp is healed.
markingPoints: Broken skin lets products in, causing stinging, reaction or infection
Checks the whole scalp and hairline in sections before applying colour
Names three valid contraindications (cuts or abrasions, infection or lice, positive skin test or past reaction, inflamed scalp)
Explains kindly, does not diagnose, and refers to a doctor where needed
Records it and rebooks for when the scalp has healed

essays.stem: Explain how the colour wheel helps a stylist choose a temporary colour to tone down an unwanted shade. Give two examples.
essays.modelAnswer: The colour wheel shows the three primary colours, red, yellow and blue, and the secondary colours made by mixing them: orange, green and violet. Colours that sit opposite each other on the wheel are called complementary colours. When they are put together they cancel each other out and make a more natural, neutral shade. A stylist uses this to tone down an unwanted shade. For example, if a client's lightened hair looks too yellow or brassy, a temporary rinse with a violet base will make it look cooler and more even. If the hair looks too orange, a blue-based product will tone it down. If there is too much red, a green-based product neutralises it. A temporary colour only adds colour on top, so it can tone the hair but it cannot lighten it. A strand test first shows how strong the effect will be on that client's hair.
markingPoints: Names primary (red, yellow, blue) and secondary colours
Explains that opposite (complementary) colours cancel each other out
Gives a correct example, such as violet for yellow
Gives a second correct example, such as blue for orange or green for red
Notes that temporary colour tones but cannot lighten, and a strand test shows the effect

essays.stem: Describe how you prepare the work area, the client and yourself before a temporary colour service.
essays.modelAnswer: First I clean and disinfect the work station and set out clean, disinfected tools: tint bowl, applicator brush or bottle, wide-tooth comb, sectioning clips and a timer. I check the product label, the shade and the date, and read the maker's instructions. I make sure the area is well ventilated, especially if sprays will be used. I check the record card for a skin test result where the maker requires one. I gown the client and put a fresh towel and a waterproof colour cape around the shoulders. I check the scalp for cuts or abrasions. I put barrier cream along the hairline and on the ears so the colour will not stain the skin. I shampoo and towel-dry the hair if the product needs it. For myself, I wash my hands, wear an apron and disposable gloves, and tie back long hair. I keep the client comfortable and tell her what I am doing at each step.
markingPoints: Clean, disinfected station and tools set out, with the product checked against the maker's instructions
Ventilation, especially for sprays
Client gowned with a fresh towel and colour cape; skin test result checked
Scalp checked, and barrier cream on the hairline and ears
Stylist wears gloves and apron and washes hands

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how you apply a temporary colour rinse or mousse to a client's hair.
essays.modelAnswer: After the consultation and any tests the maker requires, I gown and protect the client and put barrier cream on the hairline and ears. I shampoo the hair and towel-dry it so that it is damp but not dripping, as the maker says. I put on gloves. I divide the hair into four sections and clip them. Working one section at a time, I apply the rinse or mousse evenly from roots to ends, using an applicator bottle, brush or my gloved fingers. I comb it through with a wide-tooth comb so that every strand is covered and there are no patches. I wipe off any colour on the skin straight away. If the maker gives a time, I set a timer and leave it for that time only; most rinses are not rinsed out. I then style the hair as agreed, check the result in good light, show the client in the mirror and give aftercare advice.
markingPoints: Protects the client and applies barrier cream before starting
Prepares the hair as the maker says (usually shampooed and towel-dried)
Works in sections, applying evenly from roots to ends and combing through
Removes colour from the skin at once and follows the maker's timing
Styles, checks the result in good light and gives aftercare

essays.stem: Explain the extra care you take when giving a temporary colour service to natural, coily or loc'd hair.
essays.modelAnswer: Natural and coily hair is often drier and more porous in some places than in others, especially at the ends. This means it can take colour unevenly, so I do a strand test where the maker requires it or where I am unsure. I detangle gently with my fingers or a wide-tooth comb, working from the ends up, and use small sections so that the colour reaches every coil. I use a product that suits the hair: gels, mousses and hair mascara work well on twists, puffs and curls without needing heat. I avoid heavy brushing, pulling and high heat, which can break fragile hair. With locs I check that the product will rinse out, because colour and residue can build up inside the locs. I protect the hairline and edges, which are often fine and fragile. Afterwards I advise the client to moisturise and to wash the colour out gently with a moisturising shampoo.
markingPoints: Coily hair can be dry and unevenly porous, so a strand test is used
Gentle detangling with fingers or a wide-tooth comb, in small sections
Chooses a suitable product and avoids pulling and high heat
Checks the product will rinse out of locs without build-up
Protects the edges and gives moisturising aftercare

essays.stem: Explain how temporary colour products, including aerosol sprays, should be handled and stored safely, and what first aid you give if colour gets into an eye.
essays.modelAnswer: I read the label and the safety data sheet for each product and follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules. Products are kept in their original, labelled containers with the lids closed, on a shelf in a cool, dry place, away from sunlight and out of reach of children. Aerosol sprays are stored upright, away from heat, hood dryers, flames and hot tools, because the cans can burst or catch fire. I never pierce or burn an empty can. I use sprays only in a well-ventilated area, shield the client's face, and do not spray near anyone's eyes or mouth. I wear gloves and wipe up spills straight away. If colour gets into an eye, I rinse it at once with plenty of clean, cool running water, holding the eyelid open, for as long as the SDS says. I do not let the client rub it. If the eye stays sore or red, I get medical help and report the accident.
markingPoints: Follows the label, SDS, maker's instructions and Centre's rules
Original labelled containers, closed, cool and dry, out of reach
Aerosols upright, away from heat and flames, never pierced or burned
Ventilation, face shielded, gloves worn and spills wiped up
Eye: rinse with plenty of clean cool water, get medical help if it stays sore, report it

essays.stem: Describe the aftercare advice you give a client after a temporary colour, and what you write on the record card.
essays.modelAnswer: I tell the client that the colour sits on the outside of the hair and will wash out at the next shampoo. I warn her that it may rub off on pillowcases, collars and towels, and that it can run in heavy rain, sea water, swimming or a lot of sweat, which is common in our hot weather. I suggest she sleeps on a dark pillowcase or wraps her hair in a satin scarf. On very porous or lightened hair, some colour may stay longer, so I explain how to wash it out gently. I tell her to contact the salon if the scalp itches or burns. On the record card I write the date, the product and shade, the test results, how the hair and scalp looked, the timing if any, the result, and any advice given or problems. Good records help the next stylist and protect the salon.
markingPoints: Explains the colour washes out at the next shampoo
Warns that colour may rub off or run in rain, sea water or sweat
Gives practical tips (dark pillowcase or satin scarf, gentle washing)
Tells the client to report any itching or burning
Records date, product, shade, tests, timing, result and advice

essays.stem: Compare temporary, semi-permanent and permanent hair colour. Say how each works on the hair and how long it lasts.
essays.modelAnswer: Temporary colour has large colour molecules that only coat the outside of the hair, on the cuticle. It does not lighten and it washes out at the next shampoo. Rinses, mousses, gels, sprays and hair mascara are examples. Semi-permanent colour has smaller molecules that go a little way under the cuticle into the outer part of the cortex. It usually has no developer, or only a weak one, so it does not lighten, and it fades over several shampoos, as the maker says. Permanent colour is mixed with a developer (hydrogen peroxide). It opens the cuticle, goes into the cortex and forms large colour molecules there, so it cannot wash out; it lasts until the hair grows out or is cut. It can lighten and darken. Because permanent and semi-permanent colours go into the hair, a skin test is needed as the maker says, and the same care applies to any temporary product whose maker requires one.
markingPoints: Temporary: coats the cuticle, no lightening, washes out at the next shampoo
Semi-permanent: goes a little way into the hair, lasts several shampoos
Permanent: mixed with developer, enters the cortex, grows out rather than washes out
Permanent can lighten; temporary and semi-permanent cannot
Skin tests as the maker requires for each

practical1.title: Consultation, strand test and a temporary colour rinse on a training head
practical1.brief: As a group, set up a clean, ventilated colour station and give a full temporary colour rinse service on a training head (mannequin) with natural textured hair, as if it were a client. One member plays the client while another leads the consultation and fills in the record card; swap so that every member asks some of the questions. Each member then does one stage: check the scalp and hairline (on the training head, and talk through what you would look for), apply barrier cream, do a strand test on a hair swatch, and apply the rinse to one of the four sections, combing it through evenly. Follow the maker's instructions for the hair state and any timing. Finish and style the hair, check it in good light, and clean and disinfect the station and tools. Photograph each stage below, showing hands, hair and the work area only, and hand in once for the whole group with the record card.
materials: Training head (mannequin) with natural textured hair, on a clamp
Hair swatch for the strand test
Temporary colour rinse or mousse, with the maker's instructions and SDS
Shade chart and client record card
Gown, towels and waterproof colour cape
Barrier cream, disposable gloves and aprons
Tint bowl, applicator bottle or brush, wide-tooth comb, sectioning clips and timer
Shampoo, cleaning and disinfecting products for the tools
photos: The station set up, with tools laid out and members in gloves and aprons
The completed consultation and record card, with the shade chosen
The strand test swatch before and after colour
Barrier cream on the hairline and ears of the training head
The hair divided into four sections, with colour going on one section
The finished, styled result in good light
The station and tools cleaned and disinfected
checklist: Asked suitable consultation questions and recorded them, including past chemicals and allergies
Checked which tests the maker requires, and did the strand test correctly
Checked the scalp and hairline and explained what would stop the service
Protected the client area: gown, towel, cape and barrier cream on the hairline and ears
Wore gloves and an apron and followed the maker's instructions for the product
Applied colour evenly in clean sections, roots to ends, and wiped any skin staining at once
Followed the maker's timing, if any, using a timer
Gave correct aftercare advice and cleaned, then disinfected, tools and station
safety: Follow the maker's instructions, the SDS and the Centre's rules for every product
Keep the area ventilated and keep colour away from eyes; know where the eyewash or clean water is
Wear gloves and an apron; wipe spills at once so nobody slips
Do not colour over cuts, abrasions or infection on a real scalp
Store products closed and labelled, away from heat

practical2.title: Creative temporary colour on natural and textured hair, then removal
practical2.brief: As a group, plan and create a temporary colour look for a carnival or school event on natural and textured hair, then show that it washes out. Use two training heads, or members who agree to be models (photos show hair only, never faces unless the model agrees and the Centre allows it). Each member writes one part of the plan (look, products, tests, steps and aftercare) on a group plan sheet, then works on their own section of hair: twists, puffs, coils or locs. Use at least two kinds of temporary colour, such as a colour spray, coloured gel, hair mascara or a mousse, following the maker's instructions. Shield the face and work in a ventilated area for sprays. When the look is finished and photographed, each member shampoos their section of a training head or a test swatch to show the colour coming out, and notes any staining on porous hair. Clean and disinfect all tools and the work area.
materials: Two training heads with natural textured hair, or models who agree
At least two temporary colour products (spray, gel, hair mascara or mousse) with the maker's instructions
Wide-tooth combs, sectioning clips, small brushes and a face shield card
Barrier cream, gloves, aprons, towels and colour capes
photos: The group plan sheet, filled in by every member
Strand tests on swatches, before and after
Each member's section during application, with gloves on and the face shielded for sprays
The finished creative look on each training head or model's hair
A section or swatch during shampooing, showing the colour washing out
The section after drying, showing any staining
The cleaned and tidy work area
checklist: Wrote a clear part of the group plan, naming products and the tests the maker requires
Did a strand test and checked the result before working on the head
Prepared and sectioned textured hair gently, with fingers or a wide-tooth comb
Used the products as the maker says, shielding the face and working in a ventilated area for sprays
Produced an even, neat result on their own section
Showed the colour washing out and noted any staining on porous hair
